title: Daily summary net shift difference versus per-shift reconciliation
scope: Bounded semantic comparison of cashier daily-summary netting, individual shift display, and the server aggregate for one business date.
decision: For ordinary in-range monetary values and a shared day cohort, the daily net formula is consistent with the signed per-shift cash differences: server sums positive differences as overage and absolute negative differences as shortage; the daily summary subtracts shortage from overage; the shift-history row exposes each signed difference. No divergent calculation or new defect is confirmed.

behavior.server: GetBusinessDayReconciliationAsync selects shifts by BusinessDate, sums positive CashDifferencePiastres into overage and absolute negative values into shortage.
behavior.clientShift: ShiftRow.Difference retains CashDifferencePiastres; the row classifies zero/negative/positive as balanced/deficit/surplus and offers absolute difference for display.
behavior.proof: For finite values excluding signed-long overflow, sum(max(d,0)) - sum(abs(min(d,0))) equals sum(d). The daily and per-shift views are different aggregations/granularities, not duplicate business writes.

counterevidence_and_limits.cohort: Server daily summary aggregates shifts whose BusinessDate equals the day. The individual shift view may present a broader history filter; parity applies only to rows for the same business date.
counterevidence_and_limits.edge: The server calls Math.Abs on negative long values and the client exposes Math.Abs for absolute display. Signed-long minimum overflow was not tested and no valid domain range evidence was established in this comparison; no defect is asserted.
counterevidence_and_limits.intent: Different daily net and per-shift signed presentation is useful and should remain distinct unless reporting requirements say otherwise.
counterevidence_and_limits.tests: No test execution. Required unit/integration coverage: positive, negative, zero, nullable difference; mixed balanced/shortage/overage same-day shifts; total net equals sum signed differences; extreme-value policy if long bounds are supported.

recommendation: Keep the daily net KPI and individual shift signed detail separate. Add a focused test that day-level overage minus shortage equals the sum of same-day signed differences. Confirm/encode allowed monetary bounds before deciding how signed-long minimum values should be handled.
required_tests: Day with only balanced shifts yields zero net.
Shortage-only and overage-only day report expected signed net.
Mixed multi-shift day net equals sum of each same-day signed CashDifferencePiastres, with opposite deviations not hidden from detailed rows.
Document and test maximum supported cash-difference range if values can approach Int64 boundaries.

source_references.evidence: The cashier daily summary derives the day net as aggregate overage minus aggregate shortage.
The shift history row exposes signed CashDifferencePiastres and derives balanced/deficit/surplus and absolute display value.
The server scopes shifts to the requested business day, sums positive differences as overage, and sums absolute negative differences as shortage.
The API DTO exposes day-level ShiftsShortagePiastres and ShiftsOveragePiastres, which the client nets.

limitations: Static source comparison only. No runtime/API/database/visual test. Same-date aggregation contract inferred from source; cross-shift accounting policy not independently specified.
